entries.title: Fetch a URL
entries.description: Perform an HTTP GET and print the response body to stdout.

entries.title: Show response headers only
entries.description: Send a HEAD request and print only the response headers. Equivalent to -X HEAD -D -.

entries.title: Save response to a file
entries.description: Write the response body to <file> instead of stdout. Use -O to keep the remote filename.

entries.title: Follow HTTP redirects
entries.description: Follow 3xx redirects until the final response. Combine with --max-redirs to cap.

examples.description: Follow redirects from a short URL

entries.title: Allow insecure TLS (skip verification)
entries.description: Skip TLS certificate verification. Use only for local debugging — never in production.

entries.title: Send a POST request
entries.description: Force the HTTP method to POST. Usually you also need -d or --data-raw.

entries.title: Send form data with a POST
entries.description: Send a request body. Default content-type is application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

entries.title: Send a custom header
entries.description: Add a request header. Repeatable for multiple headers.

entries.title: Send HTTP basic auth credentials
entries.description: Send Basic auth. Omit the password to be prompted.

entries.title: Send a cookie
entries.description: Pass a cookie string. Use -c to also save cookies from the response. Use -b <file> to load cookies from a jar.

entries.title: Show request/response details
entries.description: Verbose mode prints the request line, headers, TLS handshake, and response status. Use --trace for a full hex dump.

entries.title: Suppress progress and errors
entries.description: Silent mode hides the progress meter and error messages. Combine with -S to still show errors.

examples.description: Pipe JSON to jq without progress noise

entries.title: Show errors even when silent
entries.description: Silent mode plus show-error. Common combo for scripting.

entries.title: Set a maximum request time
entries.description: Abort the request after N seconds. Without this, curl uses the system's default (often very long).

examples.description: 5-second timeout for a flaky health check

entries.title: Force a custom DNS resolution for a host
entries.description: Override the DNS lookup for a host. Useful for hitting a local service via its production hostname during testing.
